title: nx-app.json
description: The NX Hub app manifest: a file an app repository ships so the hub can present and install it without central curation. Publish it as a release asset named exactly `nx-app.json`, or keep it at the default branch root. See docs/PUBLISHING.md. Fields marked TRUSTED in their description are honoured only when the hub's user trusts the repository owner (settings.owners + settings.trustedManifestOwners); from any other owner they are dropped with a log line. The hub ignores unknown keys and never fails discovery over a bad manifest; this schema is stricter than the hub on purpose, so `nx manifest check` can tell you about a typo the hub would silently discard.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editor completion. Ignored by the hub.

nxApp.description: Manifest format version. 1 is the only version. Recommended, not required.

name.description: Display name of the app. Falls back to the repository name. Accepted from any owner (presentation only, escaped on render).

tagline.description: One line under the name on the card. Falls back to the repository description. Accepted from any owner.

homepage.description: http(s) URL for the app's own page. Accepted from any owner.

sandbox.description: TRUSTED. Default sandbox profile for launches when bwrap is available: `confined` = fresh tmpfs $HOME with only the install dir and `configPaths` bound rw, network shared; `offline` = confined without network; `none` = no wrapping. The user's per-app preference wins. Never applied to tarball-prefix or apk-adb artifacts.

configPaths.description: TRUSTED. Where this app keeps its user configuration. Used to bind config into a sandbox and to snapshot config before an update, an uninstall or a restore.

keepAlive.description: TRUSTED. Suggests the watchdog default for this app: relaunch it with backoff when it exits unexpectedly. Suitable for daemons, wrong for anything a user closes on purpose. The user's per-app preference wins, and a crash loop suspends it.

artifacts.description: Per-asset refinements, matched against the release's asset names. Assets you do not mention are still classified by the hub's own rules; artifacts here that match no asset are ignored.

connector.description: How to render the live status this app streams over the NX Connector bus. See docs/connector/PROTOCOL.md.

assetPattern.description: Glob matched against the release asset's file name (`*` and `?`), e.g. `Halyard-*-linux-x86_64.AppImage`. The first entry that matches an asset wins, so order from most specific to least.

label.description: Row label for this artifact, e.g. "Desktop app (Linux)". Falls back to the kind's default label. Accepted from any owner.

platform.description: TRUSTED. Which platform this asset is for. Should agree with the file name; the classifier decides it on its own when the name is clear.

kind.description: TRUSTED. Which install engine handles this asset. `tarball-prefix`, `blender-addon` and `blender-theme` only work together with the trusted-only path fields they need (`prefix`/`stripPrefix`, `addonsDir`), so an untrusted manifest cannot reach them.

packageId.description: TRUSTED. Android application id, for `apk-adb` artifacts. Used to read the installed version off the device and to launch it.

binHint.description: TRUSTED. For `archive-dir`: the executable inside the extracted tree, relative to its root. Without it the engine guesses (largest executable file / name match).

stripPrefix.description: TRUSTED. For `tarball-prefix`: leading path removed from every archive entry, e.g. `usr/`. Empty string means strip nothing.

prefix.description: TRUSTED. For `tarball-prefix`: the directory the stripped tree is written into, e.g. `~/.local`. Every written file is recorded for an exact uninstall.

addonsDir.description: TRUSTED. For `blender-addon`: the Blender add-ons directory the zip is unpacked into.

launchCmd.description: TRUSTED. What Launch runs for a `tarball-prefix` artifact, e.g. `~/.local/bin/halyard`. Without it that artifact has no Launch button.

args.description: TRUSTED. Default arguments appended when the app is launched. The user's own launch arguments still apply.

postInstallNote.description: Prose shown after this artifact installs: the one thing a user must still do. Accepted from any owner, escaped on render, and marked with its origin when the owner is not trusted.

postInstallCmd.description: TRUSTED. A single shell command offered behind a Run button beside the note, with `sudo` rewritten to `pkexec`. From an untrusted owner it is dropped — put the command in `postInstallNote` as prose instead and let the user run it.

fields.description: Labels and units for the status keys this app sends. Unlisted keys still render, as `key: value`.

key.description: The key as sent in a `status` message's `fields` object.

label.description: Human label for the value, e.g. "Boat speed".

unit.description: Unit appended to the value, e.g. "kn".

kind.description: How to format the value. `number` fields also get a sparkline of their last ten minutes — send them as JSON numbers, not strings.
